## Legacy GPT snapshots (gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4.1-nano, o1, o1-pro, o3-mini, o4-mini, gpt-image-1 etc.) shut down Oct 23, 2026; use gpt-5.6-* or gpt-image-2.5 [Verified]

### Change

Replaced the retired fine-tuning base model gpt-3.5-turbo with gpt-5.6-terra (OpenAI's listed replacement) at both fineTuning.jobs.create calls in src/index.ts. Added test-model.mjs, which checks that the old id is gone and that both calls name the new model.

Files touched:
- `dist/index.js`
- `src/index.ts`
- `test-model.mjs`

### Why

gpt-3.5-turbo was shut down on 2026-10-23, so both job-creation calls would fail.

> On April 22, 2026, we announced the deprecation of the following older OpenAI models. Access to these models was shut down on October 23, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| model-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- model-test, added by the agent: `node test-model.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_model_lookup`: fail
- `openai__openai_search_docs`: pass

Prepared before the baseline:
- Preparation changed repo files, kept out of this PR: pnpm-lock.yaml.

Test of this change: `model-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I could not confirm that gpt-5.6-terra is fine-tunable. Check the fine-tuning docs for a supported base model.
- Self-serve fine-tuning job creation ends Jan 6, 2027, and orgs without recent fine-tuned inference may already be blocked.
- Fine-tuned models derived from gpt-3.5-turbo (ft:gpt-3.5-turbo:*) are likely gone too. The repo has no downstream calls to them.
- The training data in files/input.jsonl was not checked against the new model's format.
- I did not run openai_check_request or any other provider validator.
- The test is a static source check and does not mock the SDK.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The fine-tuning base model changes. Training behaviour, cost and the resulting model quality may differ.

## Self-serve fine-tuning: active customers can no longer create new fine-tuning jobs from Jan 6, 2027 [Verified]

### Change

Added src/createJob.ts, a wrapper around fineTuning.jobs.create. It throws a clear FineTuningUnavailableError on or after 2027-01-06 and also on 400/403 API errors. Both job-creation call sites in src/index.ts now use it. Added a mocked test in test/createJob.test.ts. The self-serve end of fine-tuning has no drop-in API replacement, so this does not restore the feature.

Files touched:
- `dist/createJob.js`
- `dist/index.js`
- `src/createJob.ts`
- `src/index.ts`
- `test/createJob.test.ts`

### Why

OpenAI stops self-serve creation of new fine-tuning jobs (POST /v1/fine_tuning/jobs) on 2027-01-06. The repo's main flow will stop working then, and the code needs to fail with a clear message.

> Active existing customers will no longer be able to create new fine-tuning jobs on this date.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| createjob-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- createjob-test, added by the agent: `npx --no-install ts-node test/createJob.test.ts` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Preparation changed repo files, kept out of this PR: pnpm-lock.yaml.

Test of this change: `createjob-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No replacement approach was implemented. The product decision between prompt-based customization with a current model and another provider is left to the team.
- Whether the account has non-self-serve fine-tuning access was not checked.
- The base model gpt-3.5-turbo is retiring and was left unchanged. Its fine-tunability, and that of any substitute, was not verified.
- retrieve and listEvents for existing jobs may stop working. I did not check this.
- The provider validators (request checker etc.) were not run.
- The 400/403 mapping to FineTuningUnavailableError is a guess about how the API will reject job creation after the cutoff. It was not checked against the docs.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- On or after 2027-01-06, createFineTuningJob throws FineTuningUnavailableError without calling the API.
- Before that date, a 400 or 403 from the API is also rethrown as FineTuningUnavailableError, with the API message appended.
- Before that date, other errors pass through unchanged.

---

> * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

- package-lock.json is stale and untouched. The repo uses pnpm-lock.yaml, which was updated.

- gpt-3.5-turbo was shut down on 2026-10-23, and fine-tuning job creation ends on 2027-01-06. This migration does not address either.

- The package now requires Node >=22 at runtime.
- The SDK uses the built-in fetch instead of node-fetch.
